MOSES ORSHIO ADASU UNIVERSITY, MAKURDI Scientia Liberatio Populorum Our Vision To be the University of first choice in Nigeria, Africa and among the top 200 in the world. REV. FR. MOSES ORSHIO ADASU UNIVERSITY, MAKURDI Scientia Liberatio Populorum Our Mission To be a Centre of Excellence in creating knowledge and developing a complete person who is capable of not only responding to the cultural, social, political and economic needs of the environment but also setting the agenda for change. REV. FR. MOSES ORSHIO ADASU UNIVERSITY, MAKURDI Scientia Liberatio Populorum Our Philosophy The philosophy of the University is to seek to mould the total being by developing the mind and imparting both theoretical and practical knowledge that encourage self reliance in the individual. Frequently Asked Questions | Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi Help & Information Frequently Asked Questions Find clear answers about admissions, academic programmes, student services, research, and life at MOAUM. Search the questions Popular questions How do I apply for admission to MOAUM? Where can I find academic programmes? How do I access the student portal? Where can I get help with a university service? Browse common questions 12 answers How do I apply for admission to MOAUM? Review the current admission requirements and application instructions on the official Admissions page. Requirements and deadlines may vary by programme and admission session. Visit Admissions → Where can I find academic programmes? The Academics section of this website lists the University's programmes, undergraduate and postgraduate. Undergraduate Programmes → Postgraduate Programmes → How do I access the student portal? The Student & Staff Portal is at portal.moaum.edu.ng. It is also the first link, “Portal”, in the bar at the top of every page of this website. Open the Portal → Where can I get help with a university service? The Contact page lists the University's offices with their addresses and telephone numbers. It also has an enquiry form, and an assistant that answers from what this website publishes. Contact MOAUM → Where can I read the University's news and announcements? News, announcements and events are published on the News & Events page. It is also the “News” link in the bar at the top of every page. News & Events → Where can I learn about the University and see its campus? The About MOAUM page introduces the University, and the Visual Tour shows it in pictures and film. About MOAUM → Visual Tour → Where do I find the admission guide for my kind of programme? The Admissions section of this website has a page for each route into the University: Undergraduate Admissions Postgraduate Admissions Centre for Continuing Education Preliminary Science and Pre-Vocational & Technical Where can I find information about postgraduate study? The postgraduate programmes are listed on the Postgraduate Programmes page, and how to apply for them is set out on the Postgraduate Admissions page. Postgraduate Programmes → Postgraduate Admissions → Where can I see the academic calendar? The academic calendar is published on the Academic Calendar page of this website. View the Academic Calendar → Where can I find the faculties and departments? The Faculties & Departments page lists the University's faculties with their departments. The College of Health Sciences has a page of its own. Faculties & Departments → College of Health Sciences → How do I use the University Library online? The University Library has its own section of this website, with its services and its electronic resources. It is also the “Library” link in the bar at the top of every page. Visit the Library → Where can I find the University's research? The Research section of this website presents the University's institution-based research and its research profiles. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi News Dr. Sogo Abolarin’s Generosity Brings Mobility Relief to MOAUM Student as VC Presents Motorised Wheelchair Share Copy link Print 11 Nov Date 11 Nov 2026 The wheelchair, generously donated by Dr. Sogo Mayokun Abolarin, who is based in Canada, is intended to address the mobility challenges of the beneficiary, ease his movement around the University and enable him to participate more conveniently in his academic activities. Giving an account of how the donation came about, Mr. David Nkang Odu, a doctoral student in the Department of Public Administration, explained that he noticed Mr. Abbah's mobility challenge during the Second Semester Examinations. Moved by the student's situation, he took the initiative to seek assistance by sharing an appeal on a group platform. His appeal eventually attracted the generous intervention of Dr. Abolarin, who responded by donating the motorised wheelchair. In his remarks, the Head of the Department of Public Administration, Dr. Timothy Utile, commended Mr. Odu for his thoughtfulness and initiative in identifying the student's challenge and taking steps to secure assistance. He expressed appreciation to the donor for the humanitarian gesture, describing the intervention as a demonstration of compassion and concern for the welfare and academic progress of a fellow student. The Dean, Faculty of Administration and Management, Professor Joseph Sev, also addressed the gathering and expressed support for the initiative, which underscores the importance of collective responsibility in promoting student welfare. Speaking at the presentation, the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Timothy Terseer Alabar, applauded Dr. Abolarin for his generosity and humanitarian intervention. He equally commended Mr. Odu for his concern and initiative, noting that such acts of compassion and solidarity reflect the values the University seeks to promote. He encouraged the beneficiary to make effective use of the motorised wheelchair to facilitate his movement around the University and support his academic pursuits. In his response, Mr. Hycenth Ageh Abbah expressed profound gratitude to the Vice-Chancellor and University Management, Dr. Abolarin and everyone who contributed to making the donation possible. He described the gesture as a significant intervention that would ease his movement and make his academic journey more comfortable. The presentation underscores the importance of compassion, generosity and collective responsibility in building an inclusive university community where students, irrespective of their physical challenges, are supported and given the opportunity to pursue their academic aspirations. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi Executive Academic Leadership PROFESSOR ALABAR FORMALLY TAKES OVER AS VICE-CHANCELLOR OF REVEREND FATHER MOSES ORSHIO ADASU UNIVERSITY Following his appointment by the Executive Governor of Benue State and Visitor to the University, Rev. Fr. Dr. Hyacinth Iormem Alia (Asor Tar U Tiv), on Tuesday, 10th February, 2026, Professor Timothy Terseer Alabar has formally taken over the leadership of Reverend Father Moses Orshio Adasu University. The handover ceremony took place today at the Vice-Chancellor’s Office, where the out-going Acting Vice-Chancellor, Professor Emmanuel Ayangarumun Kenen, officially handed responsibilities of the Vice Chancellor's office to Professor Alabar. The event was witnessed by Principal Officers of the University. In his remarks, Professor Kenen expressed deep appreciation to the Governing Council, chaired by Sir Paul Chukwuma, for recommending him to serve as Acting Vice-Chancellor. He also extended his gratitude to the Governor for approving his appointment. Reflecting on his tenure, he thanked members of the university community for their cooperation, loyalty, support and encouraged them to extend the same goodwill to the new Vice-Chancellor. In his acceptance speech, Professor Alabar conveyed his profound appreciation to the Governor for the confidence reposed in him. He pledged to build his administration on three guiding pillars: intelligence, hard work and integrity. According to him, these values will shape efforts to create a more conducive environment for academic excellence. He emphasized that the core mandate of the University remains teaching, research and community service. Professor Alabar assured that student-related matters would receive priority attention, while staff welfare would be strengthened and critical facilities improved to enhance teaching, learning and research activities. Highlight of the handover was the blessing of Vice-Chancellor’s Office by Reverend Father Professor Moses Orhungur “ Our purpose is to create knowledge and to develop the complete person — men and women able to respond to the needs of their environment and to set the agenda for change. ” Prof. Timothy Terseer Alabar 8th Vice-Chancellor, Rev. The partnership Overview Walter Sisulu University (WSU) is a public university in South Africa's Eastern Cape with campuses in Mthatha, Butterworth, Buffalo City (East London) and Komani. On parts of its own website it now styles itself iYunivesithi Walter Sisulu. Its Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences is based in Mthatha. MOAUM's Centre for Advancement and Linkages records the relationship as ongoing since 2024. According to MOAUM, it covers research collaboration, staff and student exchange and joint research-grant submissions, and a WSU staff member holds a Visiting Professorship at MOAUM, teaching in Microbiology, Medical Laboratory Science and the Faculty of Clinical Sciences. The practical benefit that is verified from MOAUM's side is teaching and research support delivered at MOAUM by the Visiting Professor. No procedure, quota, funding or deadline for a MOAUM student to go to WSU on exchange has been published by either university, and WSU's website does not list MOAUM (or Benue State University) among its partners. A MOAUM graduate or scholar may still use WSU's ordinary routes, which are open to any eligible international applicant and are not a benefit of the partnership: WSU's online application for postgraduate study, which for international applicants requires a SAQA evaluation of foreign qualifications, a South African study visa and South African medical cover. The partnership Overview The University of Hildesheim is a foundation university in Lower Saxony, Germany, with about 8,000 students. Its Center for World Music is an ethnomusicological research centre that describes itself as an archive and laboratory, a place for research and study, and a meeting place for musicians. The Center has worked in West Africa for many years, including a research project on music archives in Nigeria and Ghana (2009 to 2014) and the DAAD-funded SDG Graduate School 'Performing Sustainability' with the University of Maiduguri and the University of Cape Coast (2016 to 2025). On 14 March 2024 a delegation from Benue State University, as the University was then called, signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Center for World Music in Hildesheim. According to the University of Hildesheim, the first phase is the building of a sound archive with the University and the start of joint research; teaching and student exchanges are planned for the long term. This is an institutional agreement. Neither university has published an exchange programme, a scholarship or an application procedure under it. Students who are interested should ask the Centre for Advancement and Linkages whether any exchange place or project place exists before making plans. The University of Hildesheim's general routes for international students and doctoral candidates are open to eligible applicants with or without the agreement and are listed separately below. How it began: A Memorandum of Understanding between Benue State University (now MOAUM) and the Center for World Music of the University of Hildesheim was signed at a ceremony at the Center for World Music in Hildesheim on 14 March 2024, in the presence of the University President, Prof. Dr. May-Britt Kallenrode. The University's own news says the President signed the memorandum and Benue State University countersigned it. The Benue State University delegation (13 to 15 March 2024) was Prof. Vitalis Vearumun Tarhule (Dean of the Graduate School), Prof. Elijah Terdoo Ikpanor (Director, Centre for Advancement and Linkages) and Dr. Shadrach Teryila Ukuma (Department of Theatre Arts). Nature of the collaboration Areas of collaboration The University of Hildesheim describes the agreement as follows: in a first project phase a sound archive is to be built with Benue State University and research cooperations initiated; in the long term several teaching and student exchanges are planned. It names the Centre for African Heritage and Cultural Sustainability Studies at Benue State University as the unit concerned, and records the hope of the Benue delegation that the faculties for teacher education and psychology will also benefit. During the same visit the delegation discussed funding opportunities with the DAAD in Bonn, met Hildesheim's International Office, its Research and Transfer unit and the Vice-President for International Affairs, and met the Dommuseum Hildesheim about possible cooperation on cultural heritage. The link behind the agreement is documented: Dr. Shadrach Teryila Ukuma of the Department of Theatre Arts is an alumnus of the DAAD-funded SDG Graduate School 'Performing Sustainability. Cultures and Development in West Africa', which the Center for World Music ran with the University of Maiduguri and the University of Cape Coast from 2016 to 2025. Benue State University was not a partner institution of that graduate school. No official page publishes the text of the memorandum, an exchange quota, a call for applications or any activity under the agreement after March 2024. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi International Partner University of Zagreb Zagreb, Croatia MoU signed · 2022 University A university-level bilateral cooperation agreement signed in 2022 for five years, listed by the University of Zagreb under Nigeria. What students can do Visit Partner Website (opens in a new tab) Key facts Partnership at a glance Partner University of Zagreb Country Croatia Partnership MoU signed Institutional agreement · Academic collaboration Established 2022 Student opportunities An agreement exists, but no exchange place, call or funded scheme for MOAUM students has been verified. Any exchange would need MOAUM to nominate the student to Zagreb. Research opportunities No joint project or grant with the University of Zagreb could be verified from official sources. Staff opportunities No staff exchange call or funded staff mobility for MOAUM has been verified; Benue State University is not on Zagreb's Erasmus+ KA171 partner lists for 2022 to 2026. The partnership Overview The University of Zagreb is Croatia's oldest and largest university, made up of faculties and art academies that each run their own admissions and exchange places. Its central International Relations Office keeps the list of university-level agreements and runs the exchange nomination and application system. The University of Zagreb's own website confirms that a bilateral agreement with Benue State University was concluded in 2022 for five years. That is the only fact about the relationship that an official source confirms. What the agreement has produced, which faculties are involved and whether it has been used for any mobility are not documented on either university's website. An agreement between universities is not by itself an opportunity a student can apply for. The University of Zagreb accepts exchange students only when their home university nominates them under a formal exchange programme, and students may not nominate themselves. Funded Erasmus+ exchange with Zagreb is available only to the partner institutions named in Zagreb's Erasmus+ KA171 projects, and Benue State University is not among them for 2022 to 2026. The pages below therefore separate what could follow from the agreement (which needs confirmation and nomination by MOAUM) from the University of Zagreb's general routes, and set out Croatia's visa and temporary stay rules for Nigerian citizens. How it began: A bilateral agreement between the two universities. The University of Zagreb's official list of its international agreements has, under Nigeria, the single entry: Benue State University (2022, 5 years), linked to bsum.edu.ng. Nature of the collaboration Areas of collaboration The University of Zagreb lists Benue State University (now MOAUM) among the foreign universities with which it has a signed university-level agreement, dated 2022 and concluded for five years. It is the only Nigerian university on that list and one of four African universities named there. The University of Zagreb describes such agreements in general terms as covering student and teacher exchange, exchange of administrative and professional staff, joint organisation of courses, study visits, conferences and seminars, and joint research projects. The text of the agreement with Benue State University itself is not published, so its exact clauses, the faculties involved and any exchange quotas are not verified. Partnership history 2022 Bilateral agreement between the University of Zagreb and Benue State University concluded for five years, as recorded on the University of Zagreb's list of international agreements. 2023-02-22 News report only (Blueprint newspaper): the then Vice-Chancellor is quoted as saying that through CEFTER the University had established a strong relationship with the University of Zagreb and would soon benefit in equipment, exchange of staff and training. Not confirmed on either institution's website. For students, staff and departments Student opportunities A bilateral agreement between the University of Zagreb and the University was signed in 2022, but no exchange place, scholarship or call that a MOAUM student can apply for directly has been verified. The University of Zagreb accepts exchange students only on nomination by their home university. Through the partnership Student Exchange Contact MOAUM for Current Opportunities Funding not specified Exchange study at the University of Zagreb under the bilateral agreement For: Undergraduate · Postgraduate · PhD The University of Zagreb admits exchange students who come under a formal exchange programme between their home university and Zagreb, including bilateral agreements, and it publishes a nomination and application procedure for them. Whether the 2022 agreement with Benue State University actually provides student exchange places has not been verified, so a MOAUM student cannot apply until the Centre for Advancement and Linkages confirms this and nominates the student. Eligible students Students enrolled at a university that has a formal exchange arrangement with the University of Zagreb and who are nominated by that university. Students may not nominate themselves. Study level As agreed between the two universities; not specified for the MOAUM agreement. Eligible disciplines Not specified. Courses must be ones offered by the receiving faculty or academy; Zagreb publishes a list of studies and courses in English. Duration One semester or one academic year, following Zagreb's winter and summer semester windows. Destination University of Zagreb, Croatia Funding Funding not specified Application status Contact MOAUM for Current Opportunities Application method Nomination by MOAUM is required Application Deadline: Zagreb's published windows for all incoming exchange students: nomination by the home university from 1 March to 1 May for the winter semester or full academic year, and from 1 September to 1 November for the summer semester; the nominated student's online application by 15 May and 15 November respectively. Requests for a dormitory place close on the same dates (15 May and 15 November). Academic intake: Winter semester (autumn) and summer semester (spring) · Next expected cycle: Nominations for the summer semester are accepted from 1 September to 1 November each year. Before submitting an external application, contact the relevant MOAUM faculty or the office responsible for international linkages to confirm eligibility and whether institutional nomination is required. How to apply MOAUM must nominate the student to the University of Zagreb using Zagreb's online nomination form. Only after nomination does Zagreb email the student instructions and access to its online application system. No application can be made by the student alone. 1 Step 1 : Confirm with MOAUM that the route exists Ask the Centre for Advancement and Linkages whether the agreement with the University of Zagreb covers student exchange, for which faculties and levels, and whether MOAUM is nominating students. 2 Step 2 : Choose courses at a Zagreb faculty The Learning Agreement may list only courses offered by the receiving faculty or academy. 3 Step 3 : MOAUM nominates the student The home university submits the nomination through Zagreb's online form within the nomination window. Students are not allowed to nominate themselves. 4 Step 4 : Complete Zagreb's online application After nomination, Zagreb sends the student instructions and access to its online application system; upload the required documents by the application deadline. 5 Step 5 : Arrange visa, temporary stay, insurance and housing Nigerian citizens need a visa for Croatia and, for a stay longer than 90 days, a temporary stay permit. See the visa note. Application checklist Nomination by the home university (Zagreb also publishes a student nomination letter form) Curriculum vitae in English or Croatian Learning Agreement signed and approved by the home institution (Zagreb publishes a general Learning Agreement form for bilateral exchange students from outside the EU) Transcript of Records from the home university Certificate of Enrolment from the home university Copy of the passport photo page Proof of English at B2 level if studying in English English version or certified translation of every document Travel medical insurance covering the whole stay Documents for the Croatian visa and temporary stay permit (see visa note) Eligibility Status Enrolled MOAUM student nominated by MOAUM Language English at B2 or higher for courses taught in English Agreement A formal exchange arrangement between the two universities must cover the student's field; not verified for MOAUM Academic requirements Set by the receiving faculty; courses must be agreed in the Learning Agreement. Language requirements Minimum B2 in English for study in English. Zagreb accepts a confirmation from a university English instructor on letterhead with signature and seal, or TOEFL iBT 79, IELTS 6.0, TOEIC 700 or Cambridge First Certificate. Students whose studies are entirely in English are listed as exempt; confirm with Zagreb whether a MOAUM transcript is accepted as proof. Funding and costs Funding not specified . The University of Zagreb states that students in a formal exchange programme are exempt from tuition fees. No grant, stipend or travel support for students coming under a bilateral agreement was found on Zagreb's pages, so living and travel costs should be assumed to fall on the student unless MOAUM confirms otherwise. Financial requirements: The University of Zagreb's guidance for non-EU students applying for temporary stay lists proof of financial means of at least 362.25 euros per month plus 869.40 euros for travel costs. Its rough living cost guide is about 600 euros per month in a student dormitory and about 1,100 euros per month in private accommodation. Visa, travel and stay Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs states that Nigerian holders of ordinary passports need a visa, that applications are submitted at the nearest Croatian diplomatic mission or consular post or at the visa application centre in Abuja, and that enquiries go to the Embassy of Croatia in Pretoria, South Africa. For study longer than 90 days a temporary stay permit is also required. The Ministry of the Interior states that the application for temporary stay is submitted at a Croatian diplomatic mission or consular post; students in higher education who need a visa may alternatively submit it at the police administration in Croatia. Conditions: proof of the purpose of stay, a valid travel document (valid at least three months beyond the stay), means of support, health insurance and, on a first application, proof of no criminal convictions. Temporary stay is granted for up to one year. The Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs also lists a health certificate not older than 90 days. Fees listed by the Ministry of the Interior: 46.45 euros for temporary stay, 31.85 euros for the biometric permit and 9.29 euros for its issuance. The University of Zagreb adds that visas cannot be applied for or extended inside Croatia, that documents must be translated into Croatian and certified, and that the criminal record certificate must carry an apostille and be no older than six months. Confirm the current procedure with the Embassy before applying. Official visa information ( mvep.gov.hr ) (opens in a new tab) Accommodation and insurance: The dormitory request is part of Zagreb's online exchange application; Zagreb does not guarantee accommodation but says students from overseas and from countries with a visa regime are given priority. Non-EU students must hold travel medical insurance for the whole stay with cover of at least 30,000 euros including repatriation and emergency treatment. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi International Partner German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) Bonn, Germany Programme participation · 2022 Funding agency Germany's academic exchange agency. Its In-Country/In-Region scholarships for the M.Sc. and Ph.D. in Food Chemistry were hosted at CEFTER for the 2023 to 2026 intakes. What students can do Visit Partner Website (opens in a new tab) Key facts Partnership at a glance Partner German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) Country Germany Partnership Programme participation Scholarship programme hosted at a MOAUM centre · Postgraduate funding · General funding routes to Germany (not partnership-specific) Established 2022 Main areas Food Chemistry · Food technology and post-harvest research At MOAUM Centre for Food Technology and Research (CEFTER) · Department of Chemistry Student opportunities DAAD scholarships for M.Sc. and Ph.D. Food Chemistry at CEFTER ran for the 2023 to 2026 intakes; the last call closed on 27 November 2025 and no new call is published. Research opportunities No joint research project between DAAD and the University was found; DAAD funds individuals and host programmes, and its general research grants to Germany are open to eligible Nigerian doctoral candidates and postdocs. Staff opportunities The CEFTER calls were designed primarily for university staff; DAAD's general programmes (doctoral grants, research grants, re-invitation of former scholarship holders) are open to eligible staff individually. The partnership Overview The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) is Germany's funding organisation for international academic exchange. It is not a partner university and has no memorandum of understanding with the University on record; the University's link with DAAD is that its Centre for Food Technology and Research (CEFTER) was a host institution in DAAD's In-Country/In-Region Scholarship Programme for Sub-Saharan Africa. Under that programme DAAD, with funds from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), offered scholarships for the M.Sc. and Ph.D. in Food Chemistry at CEFTER. DAAD's own calls exist for the intakes of 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026. In-Country scholarships were for candidates studying in their home country or country of residence; In-Region scholarships were for candidates from other Sub-Saharan African countries. Applicants had to apply both for admission at CEFTER and for the scholarship on the DAAD portal; the University ranked candidates and an independent DAAD selection committee made the final decision. The most recent call, for the intake beginning in October 2026, closed on 27 November 2025. As of 6 October 2026 DAAD's scholarship database does not list the University among the calls open until 12 November 2026 or among those to be published in spring 2027, so there is no open or announced round at CEFTER. This page will be updated if DAAD or CEFTER publishes a new call. Apart from the CEFTER scheme, DAAD has general programmes for study and research in Germany that eligible Nigerian graduates, doctoral candidates and academics can apply for on their own. They are listed below as general routes. They are not benefits of the University's relationship with DAAD, and the University does not nominate candidates for them. How it began: The University (then Benue State University) was accepted by DAAD as a host institution of the DAAD In-Country/In-Region Scholarship Programme Sub-Saharan Africa for two CEFTER programmes, M.Sc. and Ph.D. Food Chemistry in the Department of Chemistry. DAAD's calls refer to an Affiliate Agreement between the host university and DAAD. This is participation in a DAAD funding programme, not a memorandum of understanding with a partner university; no MoU with DAAD was found. Nature of the collaboration Areas of collaboration DAAD is a German funding organisation, not a university. From the intake of October 2023 to the intake of October 2026 DAAD published yearly calls for scholarships tenable at the University's Centre for Food Technology and Research (CEFTER) for the Master in Food Chemistry and the PhD in Food Chemistry, funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). Each call offered up to three In-Country scholarships (for people studying in their home country or country of residence) and six or seven In-Region scholarships (for nationals or permanent residents of other Sub-Saharan African countries) per degree level. DAAD paid tuition directly to the University and a monthly scholarship and allowances to the scholar. The last call (intake 2026) closed on 27 November 2025. On 6 October 2026 DAAD's scholarship database lists the calls that are open until 12 November 2026 and the calls to be published in spring 2027; the University is not among them, the programme entry now describes Master studies only, and the only Nigerian host named is the Federal University of Agriculture Abeokuta. No call for a 2027 intake at the University has been published. Separately, DAAD runs general scholarship programmes for study and research in Germany that any eligible Nigerian graduate, doctoral candidate or academic may apply for; those do not depend on the University. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi International Partner Carnegie African Diaspora Fellowship Program United States / Canada Past collaboration · 2020 Fellowship programme A fellowship programme that placed African-born scholars from U.S. and Canadian universities at African universities. The University hosted a fellow in 2020-2021. What students can do Visit Partner Website (opens in a new tab) Key facts Partnership at a glance Partner Carnegie African Diaspora Fellowship Program Country United States / Canada Partnership Past collaboration Fellowship programme participation (host institution) · Visiting diaspora scholar · Curriculum co-development · Graduate student teaching and mentoring · Collaborative research Established 2020 Main areas History · Diasporan and Heritage Studies · Arts (field of study recorded by IIE for the project) At MOAUM Department of History (Faculty of Arts) Student opportunities Students cannot apply. They benefited only indirectly, through teaching and mentoring by the visiting fellow hosted in 2021. The programme has stopped awarding fellowships. Research opportunities The 2020-2021 project included collaborative research between the visiting fellow and History staff. No joint publications or follow-on grants could be confirmed from official sources. No request can be submitted now because the programme is in its final phase and its application cycle is closed. The partnership Overview The Carnegie African Diaspora Fellowship Program (CADFP) connected African-born academics working at universities in the United States and Canada with universities in Africa. A host university in Africa proposed a project; a diaspora scholar was matched to it; and the programme paid for the scholar to spend between 14 and 90 days at the host university working on curriculum co-development, collaborative research, and the teaching, training and mentoring of graduate students. The programme is funded by Carnegie Corporation of New York (which now uses the name Andrew Carnegie Foundation) and is managed by the Institute of International Education (IIE), in collaboration with the Association of African Universities and, earlier, United States International University-Africa. Benue State University, Makurdi (now Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi) took part as a host institution. In the programme's November 2020 round it was selected to host Professor Bridget Teboh of the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth for a project in the Department of History. IIE published the project as: Straightening Curriculum, Co-developing New Course for Diasporan Studies; Teaching/ Mentoring Both Students and Junior Faculty; and Collaborative Research (spelling as published). BSU published the title as: Strengthening Curriculum in History and Co-Developing New Courses for Diasporan and Heritage Studies; Graduate Teaching/Mentoring. The BSU project was one of 74 projects selected in that round. This is a route for academic staff and departments, not for students. Students could not and cannot apply to the programme; they benefit only when a department hosts a fellow who teaches, mentors or co-supervises during the visit. The programme has stopped awarding fellowships. IIE's programme page states that the CADFP provided fellowships from 2013 through 2025, that more than 750 grants were awarded, and that it is now in its final phase, focused on strengthening its alumni community and incubating a new entity to carry on collaboration. No application cycle is open or announced, the How to Apply pages have been removed from the IIE website, and the former application portal link returns an invalid-link page. Anyone interested in future developments is asked by IIE to email AfricanDiaspora@iie.org to join the programme contact list. How it began: Benue State University was selected as a host institution in the programme's November 2020 selection round. This is participation in a fellowship programme as a host institution, not a memorandum of understanding with a university. The selection is published by the programme administrator (Institute of International Education, IIE) in its November 2020 list of selected projects and by Benue State University on its own website. Nature of the collaboration Areas of collaboration The Carnegie African Diaspora Fellowship Program (CADFP) funded African-born scholars employed at accredited universities in the United States or Canada to spend 14 to 90 days at an African host university working on curriculum co-development, collaborative research, and graduate student teaching, training and mentoring. In the November 2020 round, Benue State University, Makurdi (now Rev. Fr. Only this one hosted project could be confirmed from official sources. As of 6 October 2026 the programme is no longer awarding fellowships. The official programme page states that the CADFP provided fellowships from 2013 through 2025 and is now in its final phase, focused on its alumni community and on incubating a new entity to carry on collaboration. The programme's How to Apply pages have been removed from the IIE website and no application cycle is open or announced. The relationship is therefore a past hosting of a visiting diaspora scholar, with no current application route for the University, its staff or its students. A faculty member at a host institution submitted a Project Request to host an African-born scholar from a U.S. or Canadian university for 14 to 90 days. As of 6 October 2026 it cannot be used: the official programme page says fellowships were provided from 2013 through 2025 and that the programme is in its final phase; the How to Apply pages have been removed and no cycle is announced. The details below describe how the route worked according to the last published versions of the programme's pages (archived copies), so that staff know what to expect if a successor programme opens. Requirements, dates and how to apply Close This is the partner's own route. Any eligible applicant may use it, with or without the partnership: it is not a place reserved for MOAUM. Who is eligible Hosts: faculty at accredited, degree-conferring higher education institutions in Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania and Uganda, plus member institutions of the African Research Universities Alliance (ARUA) and partner universities of the Consortium for Advanced Research Training in Africa (CARTA). The programme's 2022 announcement describes eligible hosts as public and private higher education institutions. Institutions did not need graduate programmes to be eligible, and there was no limit on the number of Project Requests from one institution or department. Scholars: must have been born in an African country (as shown in the passport), live in the United States or Canada, hold a terminal degree, and be employed full-time at an accredited college or university in the United States or Canada; any academic rank, but postdocs were not eligible. Students could not apply in either role. Study level Not a study programme. Applicants were academic staff (hosts) and diaspora scholars. Eligible disciplines Any academic discipline (the standard All-Discipline Fellowship) Duration 14 to 90 days per project visit. Under the Flexible Fellowship model, two separate visits of at least 14 days each, not exceeding 90 days combined. Destination The host institution in Africa (for the University, Makurdi, Nigeria). The fellow travels to the host; no one from the host travels abroad. Funding Partially funded Covers: Fellow: USD 150 per day stipend, Fellow: visa costs (if required), Fellow: supplemental health insurance coverage, Fellow: round-trip international air travel, Fellow: ground transportation between the scholar's home and the North American airport, Fellow: potential opportunities to apply for supplemental funding for knowledge production activities and workshop attendance Application status Past Opportunity Application method Apply directly Application Deadline: No application cycle is open and none is announced. Next expected cycle: None published. IIE asks interested people to email AfricanDiaspora@iie.org to be added to the programme contact list to receive updates. How to apply When the route was open, the Project Request was submitted directly to IIE online by a faculty member or administrator of the host institution; no nomination by the scholar's university was needed, but the scholar had to submit a separate Scholar Application. The former portal address (https://www.onlinesubmissionportal.com/adf) now redirects to an invalid-link page. Do not present this as an open application. 1 Step 1 : Status today Applications are not being accepted. The steps below record how the route worked in its last published form. 2 Step 2 : Host prepares a Project Request A faculty member at the host institution prepared a Project Request covering one or two of the three activities: curriculum co-development, graduate student mentoring and training, and research collaboration and capacity strengthening. The request set out the institution's need, the goals of the project, the resources the host would commit, and the role of the diaspora fellow. 3 Step 3 : Name a scholar or ask to be matched The host could name a specific eligible scholar or submit without one. Without a named scholar, IIE searched its Scholar Roster for a qualified candidate; hosts could also search the roster inside the online system. 4 Step 4 : Obtain the letter of support The Project Request had to include a letter of support from an administrator at the level of Dean or higher at the host institution. A letter from an interim dean was accepted; a letter from an associate dean was not. 5 Step 5 : Scholar applies separately The scholar submitted a Scholar Application with personal statements, academic qualifications, and a letter of recommendation from a Dean (or an administrator of equal or higher level) at the scholar's own institution. 6 Step 6 : Submit online All materials, including the letter of support, were submitted through the programme's online system. 7 Step 7 : Three-tier review and notification Tier One: technical review by IIE staff for eligibility and completeness. Tier Two: discipline and regional review by committees of scholars, who recommended or did not recommend each project; hosts and scholars were notified of the recommendation status. Tier Three: the CADFP Advisory Council made the final selection from the recommended projects, and IIE notified hosts and scholars of the final status. The programme did not give specific feedback on unsuccessful requests. The partnership Overview The University of Ghana, at Legon near Accra, is Ghana's oldest university. The two universities are linked through a shared programme rather than a bilateral agreement: no memorandum of understanding between them has been published by either university, and each university's published list of partners omits the other. What is confirmed is a shared programme. Both universities host World Bank Africa Centres of Excellence. MOAUM's Centre for Food Technology and Research (CEFTER) and the University of Ghana's West Africa Centre for Crop Improvement (WACCI) are both founding members of Food for West Africa (FOOD4WA), a network of agricultural centres of excellence whose stated aims are to connect the faculty and students of its member centres, coordinate food-security research and share results through conferences and symposia. This is a network link between two centres, not an exchange agreement between the two universities. There is also a documented point of institutional contact: the University of Ghana's Regionalisation Strategy for 2023-2027 records that a former Vice-Chancellor of Benue State University advised its drafting committee on how BSU developed its own regional strategy. Nigeria is one of the ten priority countries for regional engagement named in that University of Ghana strategy. Because no partnership-specific route exists, a MOAUM student or scholar interested in the University of Ghana must use its ordinary routes for international applicants: graduate degree admission through the School of Graduate Studies, a semester or year as a visiting (non-degree) student through the International Programmes Office, research affiliation through the Office of Research, Innovation and Development, or a direct approach to a department as a visiting scholar. These are self-funded general routes and are not benefits of any partnership. How it began: No memorandum of understanding or other bilateral agreement between MOAUM/Benue State University and the University of Ghana could be confirmed from any official source. The only link confirmed is through a shared programme: both universities host World Bank Africa Centres of Excellence (ACE Impact), and MOAUM's Centre for Food Technology and Research (CEFTER) and the University of Ghana's West Africa Centre for Crop Improvement (WACCI) are both founding members of the Food for West Africa (FOOD4WA) network of agricultural centres of excellence, which WACCI's website says was officially established in December 2021. Nature of the collaboration Areas of collaboration Confirmed only through a shared programme, not a bilateral partnership. The Association of African Universities' ACE Impact directory lists CEFTER at Benue State University and three centres at the University of Ghana (WACCI, WACCBIP and the West Africa Genetic Medicine Centre). FOOD4WA's own website and a University of Ghana (WACCI) news item both name CEFTER and WACCI among the network's seven founding centres; FOOD4WA's stated objectives are to establish a network between faculty and students of the participating centres, to coordinate research on food-security themes, and to share results through conferences and symposia. In December 2022 a FOOD4WA assembly was held on the sidelines of a congress organised by CEFTER in Makurdi. Separately, the University of Ghana's Five-Year Regionalisation Strategy (2023-2027) records that a former Vice-Chancellor of Benue State University, Prof. Charity Angya, gave a virtual consultation session to the UG committee on how BSU had developed its own regional strategy. Neither university names the other as a partner. The University of Ghana's International Programmes Office publishes its exchange partners by country: the Nigerian entries are the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, the University of Calabar, the University of Ibadan, the University of Ilorin, the University of Nigeria and the University of Abuja. MOAUM's International Partnerships and MoUs page does not list the University of Ghana, and neither does the older Benue State University list of MoUs. Benue State University's Institutional Regional Strategy (August 2022) names Ghana as a priority country but the Ghanaian institution it lists as a partner is the University of Cape Coast, not the University of Ghana. The partnership Overview Zeppelin University is a privately sponsored foundation university in Friedrichshafen on Lake Constance, Germany, with state-recognised degrees and the right to award doctorates. Its teaching and research sit between business, culture and politics. The University's Centre for Advancement and Linkages records a Memorandum of Understanding with Zeppelin University, signed in 2024, covering postgraduate student exchange, joint research projects and a trans-cultural programme with the University of Pretoria. Zeppelin University has not yet published the agreement and does not list the University among its exchange partners, so it should be read as an institutional understanding, not as an open opportunity for students. What can be shown from Zeppelin University's own pages is an earlier connection through MOAUM's Department of Theatre Arts, whose staff member took part in a Zeppelin University training programme on culture and sustainable development in 2022 and 2023, and the existence of a Zeppelin University programme with the University of Pretoria, the Transcultural Caravan Network. The University's general routes for international students are described separately below; they are open with or without the agreement, and its degree programmes charge tuition fees. How it began: According to MOAUM's records and its own partnerships page, a Memorandum of Understanding with Zeppelin University was signed in 2024. No date, place, signatory or lead unit is published by either university, and no announcement of the signing was found on Zeppelin University's website, on the Transcultural Caravan website, on moaum.edu.ng or on bsum.edu.ng. Nature of the collaboration Areas of collaboration MOAUM's records describe the agreement as covering postgraduate student exchange, joint research projects and a trans-cultural programme with the University of Pretoria. None of this could be confirmed from Zeppelin University's side. Benue State University and MOAUM do not appear among the partner universities shown on Zeppelin University's International Office page, and neither name appears on the pages of its Leadership Excellence Institute Zeppelin or the Transcultural Caravan that were checked. Two things are verified. First, an earlier academic link exists: Dr. Shadrach Teryila Ukuma of Benue State University is listed by Zeppelin University as a participant in its 'Advanced Training in Co-Creating Avenues for Culture and Sustainable Development' (workshops in Ghana in December 2022, at Zeppelin University in April 2023 and in Uganda in August and September 2023), run by the Junior Professorship for Cultural and Media Policy Studies. Second, Zeppelin University does run a transcultural programme in which the University of Pretoria takes part: the Transcultural Caravan Network of its Leadership Excellence Institute Zeppelin, whose Transcultural Student Research Groups included a research trip to Pretoria in 2024 and students from the University of Pretoria again in 2026. MOAUM is not named as a participant in it. The procedure below is Zeppelin University's standard one for exchange students from its partner universities and would apply only if MOAUM is recognised as one. Before submitting an external application, contact the relevant MOAUM faculty or the office responsible for international linkages to confirm eligibility and whether institutional nomination is required. How to apply A student cannot apply for an exchange place on their own. Zeppelin University's procedure is that the student first notifies the international office of the home institution; the home university nominates the student; Zeppelin University then e-mails the student, who completes the application in an online portal. No MOAUM nomination procedure for Zeppelin University has been published. 1 Step 1 : Confirm the route exists Ask the Centre for Advancement and Linkages whether the agreement with Zeppelin University is in force, whether it includes exchange places for postgraduate students, and how MOAUM selects and nominates candidates. 2 Step 2 : Be nominated by MOAUM Zeppelin University accepts exchange students within the framework of a partnership agreement after their home university has nominated them. 3 Step 3 : Complete the online application After the nomination Zeppelin University notifies the student by e-mail and the application is completed in its online portal by the deadline. 4 Step 4 : Receive admission and apply for the visa Zeppelin University sends formal admission as an exchange student and helps with questions about the student visa and housing. Apply for the national visa for study through the German Missions in Nigeria. Required English certification: TOEFL iBT 90 or IELTS 6.5; alternatively a B2 certificate of English proficiency issued by the sending institution. Funding and costs Funding not specified . No funding for MOAUM students is published. Zeppelin University states that incoming students from its partner universities pay no tuition to it but must support themselves, with average living costs of 800 to 1,000 euros per month. It says a few scholarships, such as the Baden-Württemberg-STIPENDIUM, are available each year for incoming students; that scholarship (800 to 1,400 euros per month for 3 to 11 months) is awarded only through partnerships between Baden-Württemberg universities and their partner institutions and cannot be applied for directly. Financial requirements: No tuition for incoming students from partner universities. Living costs of about 800 to 1,000 euros per month, according to Zeppelin University. For the visa, the German Missions in Nigeria require proof of 992 euros per month, shown for up to one year. Visa, travel and stay Nigerian students need a national visa for study. The German Missions in Nigeria take applications through the Consular Services Portal of the Federal Foreign Office, followed by an appointment. Required documents include a current admission letter from the German university stating the course, start date and language of instruction, and proof of adequate financial means (992 euros per month for university studies). Zeppelin University warns that visa processing can take a long time and advises checking the embassy's website before choosing an intake. Health insurance requirements are not stated on the pages that were checked. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi International Partner University of Groningen (Rijksuniversiteit Groningen) Groningen, Netherlands MoU signed · 2024 University A Memorandum of Understanding recorded by MOAUM in 2024 for staff and student exchange for studies and research. What students can do Visit Partner Website (opens in a new tab) Key facts Partnership at a glance Partner University of Groningen (Rijksuniversiteit Groningen) Country Netherlands Partnership MoU signed Memorandum of understanding · Staff exchange · Student exchange · Research collaboration Established 2024 Student opportunities An MoU for exchange is reported by MOAUM, but no exchange place or call for MOAUM students is published. Any exchange would need a student exchange agreement and nomination by MOAUM. Staff opportunities Staff exchange is within the scope MOAUM reports; no published procedure or funding was found. The partnership Overview The University of Groningen is a research university in the north of the Netherlands. Exchange, admissions and scholarships are run partly centrally and partly by its faculties, and it has a dedicated Sub-Saharan Africa desk within its international strategy. According to MOAUM's records, the two universities signed a memorandum of understanding in 2024 for staff and student exchange for studies and research. The University of Groningen's public pages do not list the University among its exchange or Erasmus+ partners, so the practical content of the MoU still has to be confirmed with the Centre for Advancement and Linkages. An MoU is not in itself a place a student can apply for. Groningen accepts exchange students only from universities with which it has an exchange agreement, and only when the home university nominates them. A MOAUM student should therefore not apply to Groningen for exchange until MOAUM confirms that such an agreement is in force and nominates the student. Independently of the MoU, an eligible Nigerian graduate can apply for a full Master's degree at Groningen through the normal international route, and Groningen lists scholarships for which Nigerian applicants are eligible, notably the Eric Bleumink Fellowship (by nomination of Groningen's Admissions Office) and the NL Scholarship. These are general routes, not benefits of the partnership. How it began: Memorandum of understanding, according to MOAUM's own records (Centre for Advancement and Linkages, MOAUM: report on partnerships, January 2023 to November 2025). Not confirmed by any University of Groningen page or by a published MOAUM / BSU page. Nature of the collaboration Areas of collaboration MOAUM's records state that a memorandum of understanding with the University of Groningen was signed in 2024 and that it covers staff and student exchange for studies and research. This is MOAUM's statement; it could not be confirmed from the University of Groningen's website on 6 October 2026. Groningen's page on its multi-faculty exchange agreements names no African university; its list of Erasmus+ International Credit Mobility partners names universities in Ghana, Sierra Leone, Gabon, Tanzania, Kenya, Egypt and Uganda but none in Nigeria; and its Sub-Saharan Africa page names partner countries and universities without mentioning Nigeria, Benue State University or MOAUM. No Groningen faculty page naming the University was found. The University of Groningen states that to study there as an exchange student the home university must have an exchange agreement with it; whether the 2024 MoU is, or includes, such an exchange agreement, and with which faculty, is not verified. How to apply The home university's exchange coordinator must nominate the student. After nomination Groningen sends the student a registration link for its Mobility Online system. A student cannot start this alone, and MOAUM can nominate only if an exchange agreement with the relevant Groningen faculty is in force. 1 Step 1 : Confirm with MOAUM that an exchange agreement is in force Ask the Centre for Advancement and Linkages which Groningen faculty the MoU is with, whether it includes student exchange places and a tuition waiver, and whether MOAUM is nominating students. 2 Step 2 : MOAUM nominates the student Groningen requires an official nomination from the home university's exchange coordinator by the faculty's deadline. 3 Step 3 : Register in Mobility Online After nomination Groningen emails a registration link; the student enters personal data and uploads the required documents. 4 Step 4 : Immigration, housing and insurance Groningen's Immigration Service Desk applies for the entry visa and residence permit on the student's behalf. Housing must be found by the student. Example: the Faculty of Spatial Sciences accepts IELTS 6.0 or higher, TOEFL iBT 80 or higher, or Cambridge at B2 or higher, or an institutional statement of proficiency. Funding and costs Funding not specified . Groningen states that exchange students do not pay its tuition fee. No grant attached to the MoU is published. Groningen's Erasmus+ grants for incoming exchange students are limited to its 23 ICM partner universities, which do not include MOAUM, so living, travel, insurance and visa costs should be assumed to fall on the student unless MOAUM confirms funding in writing. Financial requirements: For the residence permit the Dutch Immigration and Naturalisation Service requires proof of sufficient funds; its required amount for university and higher professional education students is 1,130.77 euros per month, valid from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026. Groningen publishes its own living cost estimate on its exchange financial matters page. Visa, travel and stay Nigerian citizens need both an entry visa (MVV) and a residence permit for a stay of more than 90 days. The student does not apply to the embassy alone: the University of Groningen, as recognised sponsor, applies to the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND) on the student's behalf through its Immigration Service Desk. The IND lists a fee of 254 euros, a decision period of up to 60 days, and an appointment to collect the MVV within three months of the decision. Students must be enrolled full time and obtain at least 50 percent of the credits each year. The IND page states that a tuberculosis test in the Netherlands may be required within three months of receiving the permit; whether this applies to Nigerian nationals was not confirmed on the pages opened. Figures as shown on 6 October 2026. Official visa information ( ind.nl ) (opens in a new tab) Accommodation and insurance: The university does not own student housing. Its exchange pages point to SSH student housing (furnished rooms for up to one year, listed at 700 to 900 euros per month including utilities, reservation fee 113 euros) and to the At Home in Groningen and Hospi Housing platforms. Exchange students need health, third-party liability and other insurance. Official contact University of Groningen Sub-Saharan Africa desk: africa@rug.nl. Mobility and Scholarship Desk: msd@rug.nl. The University | Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi The University Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi Formerly Benue State University, Makurdi. A comprehensive State University dedicated to knowledge, character and the liberation of the people. Brief History From an Edict of 1991 to a comprehensive University The idea of establishing a university for Benue State was first conceived in the late 1970s by the State’s first civilian Governor, the late Aper A. Aku, and was translated into a feasible project during the administration of Governor Fidelis A. Makkah. It was brought to reality by the second civilian Governor, His Excellency the late Rev. Fr. Moses O. Adasu, who on 8 August 1991 inaugurated a 13-member Steering Committee charged with planning for the University and securing Federal Government approval for the State to run its own institution. That approval was granted on Monday, 15 February 1993, formalising a process begun through the Benue State University Edict No. 1 of 1991 — the culmination of decades of effort by successive administrations to correct a longstanding educational imbalance since the creation of Benue State in 1976. The University had by then already commenced academic activities, with an inaugural orientation held in the 1992/93 session and commissioned by the Visitor to the University, Governor Rev. Fr. Moses O. Adasu. Academic activities commenced with four foundation faculties — Arts, Education, Science and Social Sciences. Law and Management Sciences followed in 1993/94, and Environmental Sciences was added in 2014/15. The institution has since grown into a comprehensive University with fourteen faculties and colleges. In 2025 the University was renamed Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi, in honour of the cleric, statesman and former Governor whose vision shaped higher education in Benue State. It remains widely known by its founding initials, BSU. Fact File Founding law Benue State University Edict No. 1 of 1991 Academic take-off 1992/93 session Re-designated 2025 — Rev. Fr. Nigeria's National UniPod Network is a joint initiative of the Federal Government, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund), delivered through the National Innovation and Digital Transformation Partnership Programme (NIDTPP). Nigeria is the first country in Africa to take the UniPod model to scale through direct public investment. Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi, formerly Benue State University, is one of the six universities in the first cohort. Its pod is focused on Agriculture and Food Systems, a natural fit for Benue State, widely known as the Food Basket of the Nation. Step 4 Open the payment section After you have accessed the application, find and select the “Pay Application Fee” button. Step 5 Generate a payment reference On the payment page, select “Generate a reference for ₦2,000”. This creates the reference your payment needs. Step 6 Initiate payment When the reference has been generated, select “Pay ₦2,000 by Card or USSD”. Step 7 Choose a payment method Choose the payment method you prefer from those the payment page offers. Step 8 Proceed with payment Select the “Pay ₦2,000” button and follow the payment provider's instructions. Step 9 Wait for payment confirmation Wait for the application system to confirm your payment and update your application status before you continue. If your payment stays pending, contact the University before paying again. Do not assume that payment has been completed merely because money was deducted from your account. Check the transaction and application status before attempting another payment. Contact the University Application fee ₦2,000 Subject to official confirmation Step 10 Open the application form After your payment has been confirmed, select “Open the Application Form”. Step 11 Complete the required information Complete every required field accurately. IMPORTANT: Enter your Next of Kin Name. Step 12 Confirm your declaration Review your information carefully, then select the declaration checkbox only when you have confirmed that the information you supplied is correct. Step 13 Submit your application or save it for later Choose one of the two actions. Submit Application choose this when the form is complete, your information has been checked and you are ready to submit. Save and Come Back Later choose this when you need more time to complete the process. Saving an application for later is not the same as successfully submitting it. Your application is submitted only when the portal confirms it. Step 14 View and print the acknowledgement slip After you have submitted successfully, select “Acknowledgement Slip” to view it, then print it or save a copy securely. Keep your acknowledgement slip for your records and future reference. It acknowledges your application; it is not an offer of admission. It is kept only on this device: it does not retrieve, validate or submit information to the official application portal. I entered my correct JAMB Registration Number. I generated my application payment reference. I completed the ₦2,000 payment process. The application system confirmed my payment. I completed all required application fields, including Next of Kin Name. I reviewed my information and confirmed the declaration. I submitted my application successfully, or saved it to complete later. I viewed and saved or printed my acknowledgement slip after submission. I checked that my O'Level results are uploaded on JAMB CAPS. I checked whether the University's programme-change instructions apply to my original programme choice. I know where to find further official admission updates. 0 of 11 checked Need Help? Frequently Asked Questions What should I do if my JAMB Registration Number is not accepted? Enter it exactly as JAMB issued it and as it appears on your JAMB slip. The application checks the number against the list of candidates JAMB sent the University. If yours is still not accepted, contact the Admissions / Academic Affairs office through the Contact page. What should I do if my payment is still pending? Wait for the application system to confirm the payment and update your application status. Do not pay again while it is pending. If it stays pending, contact the University through the Contact page and quote your payment reference. What if money was deducted but payment is not confirmed? A deduction alone does not mean that payment has been completed. Check the transaction and your application status first. If the application still shows no confirmed payment, report it through the Contact page with your payment reference, and do not make another payment before the first one has been checked. How do I return to an application I saved for later? Go back to the application portal and sign in with the email address and password you chose when you started (“I already have an account”). Do not start a second application with the same JAMB Registration Number. A saved application has not been submitted until you select “Submit Application” and the portal confirms it. When can I access my acknowledgement slip? After the portal confirms that your application has been submitted successfully. It is not available for an application that has only been saved for later. How do I check whether my O'Level results are uploaded on JAMB CAPS? Sign in to your profile on the JAMB portal and open CAPS to see the O'Level results uploaded for you. If they are missing or wrong, complete the upload as JAMB directs. This website cannot check your CAPS record. What should I do if my original programme choice appears in the change-of-programme notices? Read the instruction for your programme under “Does Your Programme Choice Need to Change?”, confirm the alternative with the University where necessary, and make the change through the official JAMB CAPS process. Nothing on this page makes the change for you. How can I confirm the available alternative programmes? See the University's faculties and programmes on this website, and confirm what is currently available with the Admissions / Academic Affairs office through the Contact page. Where can I find the latest university admission announcements? On the university portal, and under News on this website, where admission announcements are published. Still need help? Contact the University's Admissions / Academic Affairs office. 7TH GOVERNING COUNCIL OF REV. FR. MOSES ORSHIO ADASU UNIVERSITY HOLDS INAUGURAL RETREAT IN ABUJA. | Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi News 7TH GOVERNING COUNCIL OF REV. FR. MOSES ORSHIO ADASU UNIVERSITY HOLDS INAUGURAL RETREAT IN ABUJA. Share Copy link Print Official notice From Directorate of Information & Public Relations Date 13 October 2026 The 7th Governing Council of Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi (MOAUM), led by its Pro-Chancellor and Chairman, Sir Paul Chukwuma, has successfully held its Inaugural retreat in Abuja from 1st to 4th August, 2026. The retreat was convened to strengthen the effectiveness of Council as the apex policy-making body of the University and to provide strategic direction for good governance, institutional development and effective university administration. In his welcome address, the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman, Sir Paul Chukwuma, expressed appreciation to members of Council for their commitment to the service of the University. He noted that the retreat was not merely ceremonial but a strategic platform for reflection, alignment and the development of a shared vision for the University. According to him, “As a Council, we are the apex policy-making body of this University. The quality of our governance will determine the quality of our University. This retreat therefore offers us a rare opportunity to align our vision, strengthen our synergy with Management, and lay a solid foundation for a University that is globally competitive, digitally driven, transparent and responsive to societal needs.” At the end of extensive deliberations, Council resolved as follows: Strengthening Governance and Communication. Council reaffirmed its commitment to effective governance through improved communication and collaboration among Government, Council and Management, with a view to ensuring efficient administration and the attainment of the University's strategic objectives. Revitalisation of ICT and Digital Transformation. Council approved measures to revitalise the University's Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Unit for improved service delivery. The measures include the provision of relevant facilities, engagement of appropriate personnel and activation of the ICT Board to provide effective oversight. Council also directed the development of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy to guide the responsible and ethical use of AI by staff and students. Support for Innovation and Externally Funded Projects. Council received a briefing from Dr. Joshua Attah, Coordinator of Special Projects at the National Universities Commission (NUC), on World Bank-funded projects and related opportunities. Council reaffirmed its support for the Centre for Food Technology and Research (CEFTER) and other externally funded centres and projects. It further resolved to strengthen mechanisms for the sustainability of such projects and establish a central coordinating unit for externally funded projects to promote efficiency, accountability and transparency. Enhanced Compliance and Capacity Building. As part of efforts to strengthen transparency, accountability and adherence to global best practices, Council resolved to engage relevant anti-corruption and regulatory agencies, including the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), for capacity-building programmes on financial management, procurement procedures and regulatory compliance. The Council expressed appreciation to all stakeholders for their continued support and reiterated its commitment to repositioning Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University for academic excellence, innovation, good governance and quality service delivery. Published by Directorate of Information & Public Relations Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi News SALE OF ADMISSION FORMS INTO PART-TIME DEGREE PROGRAMMES AND CERTIFICATE COURSES OF THE CENTRE FOR CONTINUING EDUCATION, REV. FR. MOSES ORSHIO ADASU UNIVERSITY, Share Copy link Print Official notice From Directorate of Information & Public Relations Date 10 November 2026 SALE OF ADMISSION FORMS INTO PART-TIME DEGREE PROGRAMMES AND CERTIFICATE COURSES OF THE CENTRE FOR CONTINUING EDUCATION, REV. FR. MOSES ORSHIO ADASU UNIVERSITY, MAKURDI FOR 2026/2027 ACADEMIC SESSION (A) Applications are invited from suitably qualified candidates for admission into the following Part-Time degree programmes: B.A. French, B.A Linguistics, B.A Philosophy, B.A Religious Studies, B.Sc. Public Administration, B.Sc Economics, B.Sc Sociology, B.Sc Business Administration, B.Sc Accounting, B.Sc Marketing, B.Ed Christian Religious Studies, B.Ed English Education, B.Ed Social Studies and Civic Education, B.Ed Guidance and Counseling, B.Ed Educational Management, B.Ed Early Childhood Education. Mode of Application: Candidates are to process their admission on the university online portal: bsum.edu.ng using their JAMB registration number. Candidate without JAMB registration number can register using their NIN. After processing admission through the JAMB portal, candidates are to pay admission processing fee of Ten Thousand Naira (N10, 000.00) only via the university REMITA platform. Candidates are to proceed to the Centre for Continuing Education (CCE) for further directives. Entry Requirements: Applicants may possess any of the following qualifications for admission: (i) Entry into 100 level: Minimum of five (5) O/level passes at credit level in relevant disciplines including English Language and Mathematics. (ii) Entry into 200 level: IJMB, National Diploma (ND), National Certificate of Education (NCE), including O/Level requirement in (1) above. REV. FR. MOSES ORSHIO ADASU UNIVERSITY, MAKURDI CENTRE FOR CONTINUING EDUCATION IN COLLABORATION WITH SECURITY AND FORENSIC STUDIES NIGERIA-ABUJA Admission into Certificate Prorammes (B) Applications are invited from suitably qualified candidates for admission into the following Certificate Courses (1) PROFICIENCY CERTIFICATE COURSE (PCC) This offers proficiency course in Security Forensic Studies. Mode of Application: Candidates are to process admission form at the cost of ten thousand naira (N10, 000.00) only at the Centre for Continuing Education (CCE). Entry Requirements: Applicants shall possess at least four (4) credit passes at SSCE, WAEC, Trade Test or NABTEB. Serving military/ paramilitary officers with requisite qualifications are eligible for admission into the programme. Duration: The programme is run on part-time basis for two semesters (6 months). (2) BASIC CERTIFICATE COURSE (BCC) This offers certificate in Basic Intelligence and Detective Studies Mode of Application: Candidates are to process admission form at the cost of ten thousand naira (N10, 000.00) only at the Centre for Continuing Education (CCE). Entry Requirements: Applicants shall possess either OND, NCE. HND. Bachelor’s degree in all fields is added advantage. Serving military/ paramilitary officers with requisite qualifications are eligible for admission into the programme. Duration: The programme is run on part-time basis for two semesters (6 months). (3) ADVANCED PROFESSIONAL COURSE ON SECURITY AND FORENSIC STUDIES (with options in): Medical Forensic Studies, Investigation/ Intelligence Forensic Studies, Accounting/Auditing Forensic Studies, Cyber Security and Forensic Studies, Legal/ Litigation Forensic Studies. Mode of Application: Candidates are to process admission form at the cost of ten thousand naira (N10, 000.00) only at the Centre for Continuing Education (CCE). Entry Requirements: Applicants may possess any of the following: RN, OND, and NCE. HND, Bachelor’s degree in all fields or Fellows of other Professional Bodies is added advantage. Serving military/ paramilitary officers with requisite qualifications are eligible for admission into the programme. Duration: The programme is run on part-time basis for two semesters (6 Months). (4) EXECUTIVE MANAGERIAL COURSE ON PEACE/RECONCILIATION AND SECURITY STUDIES Mode of Application: Candidates are to process admission form at the cost of ten thousand naira (N10, 000.00) only at the Centre for Continuing Education (CCE). Entry Requirements: OND, NCE, HND or Bachelor’s degree or Advanced Professional Course or any equivalent from other Professional bodies. Security Management experts are also eligible for admission. Duration: The programme is run on part-time basis for two semesters (6 months). Note: Application forms are available from 5th November 2026. Candidates may visit the Centre for Continuing Education or call, 08066711643, 08118242036, 08027406102, 07037897904 for further enquiries.
